about: The classes NeoCity Academy offers. The plan, the Classes tab and the counselor pick ONLY from this list, so add every class the school offers. Each class: id (unique, lowercase-with-dashes), name (exactly as the school writes it), department, pathway (Engineering, Biodesign, Artificial Intelligence, or null), level (AP, AICE, Honors, Career & technical, Core, Dual enrollment), area (Math, Science, Computer science, Engineering, Health, English, Social studies, World language, Arts, Business), grades (the grades it's offered in; [] when the school doesn't say), follows (ids of classes to take first), certifications, description (one or two plain sentences for students), source (where it came from).

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence in the World
courses.description: An introduction to AI: what counts as intelligent behavior, how AI connects to computer science, its history and real uses, the data and algorithms behind AI decisions, hands-on machine learning activities, and AI ethics.

courses.name: Foundations of Machine Learning
courses.description: Builds the math behind AI and machine learning algorithms, along with coding and software development skills, through hands-on lab work.

courses.name: Applications of Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Explores the methods and software used to build AI models and applications from data sets, with hands-on lab projects.

courses.name: Digital Information Technology
courses.description: Core computer skills for school and business: databases, spreadsheets, presentations, email, word processing, the internet, HTML and web page design, using industry-standard software.

courses.name: AP Computer Science Principles
courses.description: A college-level introduction to computer science: designing algorithms and programs, working with data and abstraction, how computers and the internet work, and computing's impact and ethics.

courses.name: Principles of Biomedical Science
courses.description: Explores the wide range of biomedical careers through design, data analysis, disease outbreaks, clinical empathy and health promotion, building skills that carry into any career.

courses.name: Human Body Systems
courses.description: Medicine in action through real-world cases: diagnosing and treating patients at an outpatient center, keeping people safe on remote adventure trips, and designing lab investigations on growth and aging.

courses.name: Medical Interventions
courses.description: Follow the life of a fictional family to investigate how to prevent, diagnose and treat disease, with projects like designing a prosthetic arm.

courses.name: Biomedical Innovation
courses.description: Builds on the earlier Biodesign classes: design your own solutions to the biggest health challenges of the 21st century.

courses.name: Applied Engineering Technology 1
courses.description: An introduction to engineering and engineering technology, with the math, science and technology behind them, to prepare for engineering in college.

courses.name: Applied Engineering Technology 2
courses.description: Uses engineering math and science to design solutions to real-world problems, and looks at how technology and design shape each other.

courses.name: Applied Engineering Technology 3
courses.description: Hands-on projects in mechanical, electrical, civil and environmental engineering.

courses.name: Applied Engineering Technology 4
courses.description: Capstone: pick a real-world challenge, then research, design, test and present your solution to a panel of engineers.

courses.name: Algebra 2 Honors
courses.description: Complex numbers, polynomial and rational expressions, graphing many kinds of functions, nonlinear systems, transformations and inverses, and basic probability.

courses.name: Geometry Honors
courses.description: Proofs about shapes, congruence and similarity, measuring 2D and 3D figures, equations of circles, and right-triangle trigonometry.

courses.name: AP Precalculus
courses.description: Prepares you for college math and science by mastering functions and modeling; useful for STEM, health, social science and data science careers.

courses.name: Calculus 1 Honors
courses.description: Limits and continuity, derivatives and their uses, analyzing graphs, and integrals with their applications.

courses.name: AP Calculus AB & BC
courses.description: College-level calculus built around change, approximation and analyzing functions, explained with graphs, numbers, equations and words.

courses.name: AP Statistics
courses.description: Collecting, analyzing and drawing conclusions from data: exploring data, sampling and experiments, probability and simulation, and statistical inference.

courses.name: Chemistry 1 Honors
courses.description: Chemistry in more depth and at a faster pace than regular Chemistry 1, with lab work at the center.

courses.name: AP Biology
courses.description: College-level biology: evolution, how cells work, genetics, how information passes between generations, ecology, and how living things interact.

courses.name: AP Chemistry
courses.description: College-level chemistry through lab investigations: atomic structure, bonding, reactions, kinetics, thermodynamics and equilibrium.

courses.name: AP Environmental Science
courses.description: How natural systems work together, and analyzing environmental problems (natural and human-made) using several sciences.

courses.name: AP Physics 1
courses.description: Algebra-based college physics: motion, forces, energy, momentum, rotation, electricity, circuits and waves.

courses.name: AP Physics C
courses.description: Calculus-based college physics (Mechanics): motion, Newton's laws, energy and power, momentum, rotation, oscillations and gravity.

courses.name: AICE General Paper
courses.description: Read, write and argue about economic, scientific, environmental, technological and cultural issues.

courses.name: English 2 Honors
courses.description: Advanced reading, writing, speaking and listening with challenging texts, to get ready for college and careers.

courses.name: AP English Language
courses.description: Write research-backed arguments and analyze how nonfiction texts and images persuade.

courses.name: AP English Literature
courses.description: Close reading of fiction, poetry and drama, and essays that interpret literature.

courses.name: AP Seminar
courses.description: First course of AP Capstone: investigate real problems across subjects, compare perspectives, and present your ideas alone and in teams.

courses.name: AP Research
courses.description: Second course of AP Capstone: a yearlong research project on a question you choose, ending with a 4,000 to 5,000 word paper you present and defend.

courses.name: AP World History: Modern
courses.description: World history from 1200 to today, thinking like a historian.

courses.name: AP United States History
courses.description: U.S. history from about 1491 to today, thinking like a historian.

courses.name: AP European History
courses.description: European history from about 1450 to today, thinking like a historian.

courses.name: AICE Psychology
courses.description: Biological, cognitive, social and learning psychology, plus two of clinical, consumer, health or organizational psychology. No psychology background needed.

courses.name: AP US Government and Politics
courses.description: College-level U.S. government: the Constitution, civic participation, how policy is made, and analyzing political data and texts.

courses.name: United States Government Honors
courses.description: How U.S. government institutions and political processes work, and their impact on American society.

courses.name: AP Microeconomics
courses.description: College-level economics of individual choices: scarcity, markets, costs and benefits, production and public policy, using graphs and data.

courses.name: Economics Honors
courses.description: National and world economic systems, banking and monetary policy, economic theories, and the business cycle.

courses.name: Spanish 1
courses.description: An introduction to Spanish and its cultures, focused on speaking and understanding, with a start on reading and writing.

courses.name: Spanish 2
courses.description: Builds on Spanish 1: more listening, speaking, reading and writing, with speaking as the main goal.

courses.name: Spanish 3 Honors
courses.description: Grow your vocabulary and conversation through discussing readings and everyday topics.

courses.name: AP Spanish Language and Culture
courses.description: Taught almost entirely in Spanish: real-life communication, understanding and being understood, more than grammar drills.

courses.name: Digital Media/Multimedia Foundations
courses.description: Presentation production, digital photography and photo editing, with industry certifications in Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator.
